# API Checklist: Team Kanban Board

**Purpose**: Validate that the REST API requirements in `contracts/api.md` are complete,
clear, consistent, and unambiguous enough to implement and generate a fully typed client from.
**Created**: 2026-11-19
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [contracts/api.md](../contracts/api.md)
**Focus**: API / Contract requirements quality — Standard PR-reviewer gate

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on
feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.
Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is
satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for
requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

---

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are response schemas defined for every error status code (400, 401, 404, 422) on all 13 endpoints, not just the globally shared error section? [Completeness, Contracts §Common Error Responses]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is pagination documented for all list endpoints (GET /projects, GET /projects/{id}/tasks, GET /tasks/{id}/comments) or is infinite list behaviour explicitly accepted? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are all HTTP methods for each resource explicitly enumerated, including which methods are intentionally absent (e.g., DELETE /projects, PUT /tasks)? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is the OpenAPI schema endpoint (GET /openapi.json) itself documented as a formal contract surface that the client generation step depends on? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are sort-order requirements specified for every list endpoint (projects, tasks, comments) using consistent terminology? [Completeness, Contracts §Projects, §Tasks, §Comments]
- [ ] CHK006 - Is the full field set of `TaskDetailResponse` explicitly listed and distinguished from `TaskResponse`? [Completeness, Contracts §GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}]
- [ ] CHK007 - Are requirements defined for the `GET /health` endpoint's behaviour when the database is unreachable but the application process is healthy? [Completeness, Contracts §Health]

---

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 - Is "non-whitespace" for comment `body` defined with a precise rule (e.g., strip-then-min-length-1) rather than relying on implementer interpretation? [Clarity, Contracts §POST /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/comments]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is "at least one field must be provided" for `PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` specified with an explicit list of which fields count toward that minimum? [Clarity, Contracts §PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is the ISO 8601 UTC format requirement for all `created_at` fields specified with a canonical example and timezone designator (`Z` vs `+00:00`)? [Clarity, Contracts §Timestamps]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is the X-User-Id validation rule (must be one of the five seeded IDs, 1–5) stated at the per-endpoint level or only in the global Conventions section? [Clarity, Contracts §Authentication]
- [ ] CHK012 - Is "send null to clear" for `description` in `PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` explicitly specified, or is it ambiguous whether omitting the field vs. sending null differ in semantics? [Clarity, Contracts §PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}]
- [ ] CHK013 - Is the `column` enum (`todo`, `in_progress`, `in_review`, `done`) defined in one canonical location and referenced consistently across task creation, task update, and response schemas? [Clarity, Contracts §Tasks]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is the term "immediately" in task creation and board update acceptance scenarios quantified with a latency threshold, or is it left unspecified? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 2]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is "ordered by `created_at` descending" (projects) vs "ascending" (tasks, comments) distinction unambiguous and justified in the contracts? [Clarity, Contracts §Projects, §Tasks, §Comments]

---

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK016 - Is the X-User-Id header requirement consistently applied to all write operations (POST, PATCH, DELETE) and consistently absent from all read operations (GET) across all 13 endpoints? [Consistency, Contracts §Authentication]
- [ ] CHK017 - Are embedded user objects (`creator`, `assignee`, `author`) consistently structured as `UserResponse` (id + name + role) in every response schema that includes them? [Consistency, Contracts §Response Schemas]
- [ ] CHK018 - Are 422 validation error response bodies consistently structured (using the `detail` array with `loc`/`msg`/`type`) for all endpoints that perform input validation? [Consistency, Contracts §Common Error Responses]
- [ ] CHK019 - Does `PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` response omit `comments` consistently with the note "use GET for full detail" — and is this asymmetry between task list and task detail responses documented explicitly? [Consistency, Contracts §PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are the HTTP success status codes (200 vs 201 vs 204) applied consistently and correctly across all creation (POST → 201), update (PATCH → 200), deletion (DELETE → 204), and read (GET → 200) endpoints? [Consistency, Contracts §Endpoints]

---

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK021 - Are latency requirements for the API layer specified per endpoint or inherited by reference from success criteria (SC-001: column move < 5 s, SC-004: board load < 3 s, SC-005: task creation < 60 s)? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK022 - Can the "valid X-User-Id header required" 401 response requirement be objectively verified — is there a specified test for the boundary between valid (1–5) and invalid (0, 6, non-integer) values? [Measurability, Contracts §Authentication]
- [ ] CHK023 - Are the validation error requirements for `title` (max 100 chars), `description` (max 2000 chars), and `body` (max 2000 chars) expressed as objectively testable acceptance criteria with exact boundary values? [Measurability, Contracts §Tasks, §Comments]

---

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK024 - Are requirements defined for concurrent `PATCH` requests targeting the same task (e.g., two users simultaneously moving it to different columns)? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK025 - Are requirements specified for `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/tasks` when the project exists but has zero tasks (empty array vs. 404)? [Coverage, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK026 - Are requirements specified for `GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}/comments` when the task exists but has zero comments (empty array vs. 404)? [Coverage, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK027 - Is the behaviour of `PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` with an empty JSON body `{}` explicitly specified (should it return 422 or is it silently ignored)? [Coverage, Edge Case, Contracts §PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}]
- [ ] CHK028 - Are requirements defined for all cascade scenarios — specifically, what the API returns if a task's parent project no longer exists (even though project deletion is deferred)? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK029 - Are recovery/rollback requirements specified for partial failures during task creation (e.g., the row is inserted but the response fails to serialize)? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Gap]

---

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK030 - Is behaviour specified for `X-User-Id` values that are syntactically valid integers but outside the seeded range (e.g., 0, 6, 999) — distinct from non-integer values? [Edge Case, Contracts §Authentication]
- [ ] CHK031 - Is the maximum number of tasks per project, or comments per task, specified or explicitly left unbounded? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK032 - Is the `description` field behaviour on `PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}` explicitly specified for three distinct states: omitted (unchanged), `null` (cleared), and empty string (should this be rejected or treated as null)? [Edge Case, Clarity, Contracts §PATCH /api/v1/tasks/{task_id}]

---

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK033 - Are rate limiting requirements (per-IP, per-user, per-endpoint) specified for the API, or is the absence of rate limiting in phase 1 explicitly documented? [Non-Functional, Gap]
- [ ] CHK034 - Is the API versioning strategy (`/api/v1/` prefix) documented with a stated policy for what triggers a version increment and how clients are notified? [Non-Functional, Gap]
- [ ] CHK035 - Are CORS requirements specified for the frontend-to-backend communication (allowed origins, methods, headers including `X-User-Id`)? [Non-Functional, Gap]
- [ ] CHK036 - Are payload size limits (maximum request body bytes) specified for endpoints that accept large text fields (description up to 2000 chars, comment body up to 2000 chars)? [Non-Functional, Gap]

---

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK037 - Is the assumption that seeded user IDs are 1–5 and immutable documented at the contracts level (not just in `data-model.md`) so client implementers know the valid X-User-Id range? [Assumption, Contracts §Authentication]
- [ ] CHK038 - Is the dependency on a running backend (port 8000) for `npm run generate-client` documented as a formal prerequisite, with failure behaviour specified if the backend is unreachable? [Dependency, Contracts §Frontend Client Generation]
- [ ] CHK039 - Is the assumption that project deletion is out of scope in phase 1 documented at the contracts level (not only in the spec) so API consumers know not to expect a DELETE /projects endpoint? [Assumption, Gap]

---

## Security Deviation Tracking (ADR-0001)

- [ ] CHK040 - Does `contracts/api.md` document that `X-User-Id` is not cryptographically verified in phase 1, so API consumers understand the trust boundary? [Security, ADR-0001, Completeness]
- [ ] CHK041 - Is the time-bounded nature of the X-User-Id deviation referenced in contracts so that the phase 2 auth migration obligation is visible to contract consumers, not only to constitution reviewers? [Security, ADR-0001, Traceability]
- [ ] CHK042 - Are the 401 Unauthorized error requirements explicitly specified for every individual write endpoint (not only in the global Conventions section), ensuring no write path silently accepts an unauthenticated request? [Security, ADR-0001, Completeness, Contracts §Authentication]

---

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK024 (concurrent PATCH), CHK029 (partial failure recovery), and CHK033 (rate limiting) are likely intentional phase 1 gaps — confirm and document if so
- Items CHK040–CHK042 track the constitution Security-First deviation formally accepted in ADR-0001
